thesis: Microsoft supports a funded-compounding purchase: operating income grew 21%, adjusted EPS 22%, and annual cash FCF remained $66.987bn despite nearly doubled capex. Rising CFO and a $36.549bn liquid surplus excluding leases give the bull measured financing and growth support at 30.63x OpenAI-adjusted FY earnings. The 6.5% FCF decline and premium valuation constrain conviction, but imperfect conversion does not outweigh the large positive cash engine.
strongest_counterexample: Cash FCF declined while earnings grew, and its cash-PP&E definition excludes noncash equipment and some lease demands; poor incremental cloud returns could compress the premium despite accounting growth.
invalidation_conditions: Next comparable annual cash FCF below $66.987bn alongside no year-on-year operating-income growth would undermine the funded-compounding basis.
A comparable year with cash PP&E exceeding CFO, from $115.948bn versus $182.935bn, would invalidate the positive cash-funding foundation.
decisive_factors: CFO increased from $136.162bn to $182.935bn, establishing actual internal funding growth.
Adjusted EPS basis avoids investment-gain cheapness; technical extension argues for deliberate timing.
